patients.label: 14-year-old boy with sudden painless bilateral vision loss, right upper limb weakness and MRI-defined optic neuritis

identity_evidence.quote: A 14-year-old boy visited the neurology outpatient department (OPD)

attribution_limitations: The conclusion refers to neuromyelitis optica in a general sentence about early neurophysiotherapy, while the case itself is described as optic neuritis; neuromyelitis optica is not stated as this patient's diagnosis.
Visual acuity is printed as two values without saying which eye each belongs to, and the Snellen chart result is printed separately without eye or relation to the acuity values.

"for 10 days" closes the complaint clause; it is read as governing blurring, dizziness and head rolling, although it could also attach only to "while returning to school". Table 1 dates diminution of both eyes 10/10/2023, right upper limb weakness 16/10/2023 and admission 18/10/2023, while the text gives weakness "for two days" and blurring "for 10 days" at the outpatient visit, whose date is not stated; the durations and dates do not reconcile arithmetically to a single visit date.
The text does not state the findings of the post-rehabilitation MRI; Figure 2 is only captioned as the post-rehabilitation MRI and the arrow drawn on it is not explained.

The Discussion states that the study investigated visual scanning exercises in stroke patients with eye movement problems, which does not describe this single boy with optic neuritis; it is treated as unlabelled discussion, not patient fact.
